---
title: "Scrape: social platforms"
engine: knitr
---

The "List of most popular social platforms" page has three tables: a 1-row stub, a 5-row table of video-calling apps with a `No.` ranking column, and the 36-row table we actually want. All three share overlapping column names, so instead of matching on a header string we pick the table that has `Country[b]` but not `No.`.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

In R, `httr2` fetches the page, `rvest::html_table()` parses every table on it, and `Filter()` keeps the one with a `Country[b]` column and no `No.` column.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-social-r
#| eval: false
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(readr)

html <- request("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_social_platforms") |>
  req_user_agent("wikimill-project/0.1") |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_html()

tables <- html_table(html)
social <- Filter(\(t) "Country[b]" %in% names(t) && !"No." %in% names(t), tables)[[1]]
names(social) <- c("name", "company", "country", "launched", "monthly_active_users", "other_metrics")
write_csv(social, "data/social_platforms.csv")
head(social)
```

## Python

In Python, `requests` fetches the page, `pandas.read_html()` parses every table, and `next()` returns the first one that passes the same check.

```{python}
#| label: scrape-social-py
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_social_platforms"
html = requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}).text

tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(html))
social = next(t for t in tables if "Country[b]" in t.columns and "No." not in t.columns)
social.columns = ["name", "company", "country", "launched", "monthly_active_users", "other_metrics"]
social.to_csv("data/social_platforms.csv", index=False)
social.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-note}

## Which language should I use?

Both versions pick the table by its column names, so the code is nearly line for line the same:

* `rvest::html_table()` returns a list of tibbles, and `Filter()` tests each one's `names()`.

* `pandas.read_html()` returns a list of DataFrames, and a generator expression tests each one's `columns`.

:::

These chunks are shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `Rscript src/scrape_social.R` or `python src/scrape_social.py` from the project root to refresh `data/social_platforms.csv`. See [clean_social.qmd](clean_social.qmd) for the next step.
